heading: INT. WRESTLING GYM - EMPTY LOCKER ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. WRESTLING GYM - EMPTY LOCKER ROOM - NIGHT
A concrete locker room beneath a high school gym.
Rows of dented lockers.
A long bench.
A whiteboard with half-erased plays.
Fluorescent tubes buzz.
A cheap phone sits on the bench, facedown, silent.
No one is here.
Rain drums on the roof above.
Then footsteps on the stairs.
COACH ODETTE BRANNIGAN, fifties, enters, shaking water from a whistle lanyard.
She wears a windbreaker with the school's faded crest.
She is soaked and she doesn't care.
She crosses to the bench, picks up the phone, studies it, sets it down.
The phone buzzes.
She looks at the screen.
She does not answer.
It goes to voicemail.
A recorded voice fills the room.
Hey, Odette. It's you. It's me. Yesterday you. Listen, you're going to want to quit tonight.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: Don't.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: Don't say "don't." You always say "don't." Just listen.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: She sits on the bench, elbows on knees.
Twenty-six years. Twenty-six years of whistles, of weigh-ins, of boys crying in showers.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: Of boys crying in showers.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: And what do I get? A losing season. A board meeting. A letter.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: The letter said "restructure."
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: I know what it said. It said, "Thank you for your service, please clear your locker."
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: She stands, goes to a locker at the end of the row, spins the dial, opens it.
It is full of ribbons, photographs, a dented trophy.
She takes none of it.
Eleven state champions. Forty-four all-conference. One kid who made the Olympic trials and cried so hard he forgot his shoes.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: He forgot his shoes, Odette. You drove them to Colorado.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: Shut up.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: You drove eleven hours with a pair of shoes on the passenger seat. And he wrestled barefoot because they were the wrong size.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: He still won.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: He still won.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: She takes a deep breath.
She closes the locker.
She leans her forehead against it.
I'm tired.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: I know. That's why you recorded this. So that I would say it to you when you were tired enough to hear.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: What do I say to them?
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: Nothing. You just show up. Tomorrow at six. Same as always. Let the board send their letter.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: They'll fire me.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: Probably.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: Then why?
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: Because the boys will be there at six. And they're waiting for you to say go.
units.name: COACH ODETTE

units.text: A pause.
The voicemail ends with a soft beep.
Odette picks up the phone and holds it to her chest for a long moment.
She lays it on the bench.
Then she goes to the whiteboard, picks up a marker, and writes in large block letters: "6 AM."
Go.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: She turns off the light.
